units: Peah VII, 3 איזהו פרט הנוֹשֵׁר וכ׳ by pereṭ (Lev. XIX, 10) is understood that which drops on cutting grapes.

<cite ref="Beitzah 2b:14">Bets. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>פירות הנוֹשְׁרִין</he> fruit which drops from the tree (on the Holy Day). Y. ib. I, beg. 60ᵃ <he>ספק מהיום נָשְׁרוּ וכ׳</he> where it is doubtful whether they fell off to-day (on the Holy-Day) &c.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 10">Gen. R. s. 10</cite>, v. <cite ref="N01328"><he>נָשַׁל</he></cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 22:4">Sabb. XXII, 4</cite> (<cite ref="Shabbat 146b:11">146ᵇ</cite>) <he>מי שנשרו כליו בדרך</he> (<he>במים</he>) if one’s garments (cloak) fell into a puddle on the road.

senses.gloss: to let fall, drop. Ib. 67ᵃ אילן שמַשִּׁיר פירותיו a tree that drops its fruit prematurely.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Nazir 6:3">Naz. VI, 3</cite> <he>מפני שמַשֶּׁרֶת וכ׳</he> because it causes falling out of the hair. Y. Peah VIII, 20ᵃ bot. <cite ref="M02978"><he>מַשִּׁיר</he></cite> (not <he>משייר</he>), v. <cite ref="M00796"><he>מַחֲבוֹא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 14:4">Midr. Till. to Ps. XIV</cite> <he>עתיד … להַשִּׁירוֹ</he> the Lord will cause him to drop, v. <cite ref="N00298"><he>נוֹבֶלֶת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Ketubot 6b:2">Keth. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>אע״פ שמַשִּׁיר צרורות</he> although (by walking through the breach) he causes pebbles to break loose; Y. Ber. II, 5ᵇ top <he>אפי׳ מַשֶּׁרֶת צרורות</he> even if the wall is so brittle as to drop &c.; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Beitzah 35b:10">Bets. 35ᵇ</cite> <he>מַשִּׁירִין</he>, <cite ref="M01442"><he>מַנְשִׁירִין</he></cite> (prob. to be read: <he>מְנַשְּׁרִין</he> as versions of <he>מַשִּׁילִין</he>, v. <cite ref="N01328"><he>נָשַׁל</he></cite>).—
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 4:2">Esth. R. to I, 14</cite> <he>ומַשִּׁירָן</he>, v. <cite ref="K01276"><he>כַּרְשׁינָה</he> II</cite>.

senses.gloss: (cmp. Assyr. našâru, Del. Assyr. Handw., p. 487) to tear, lacerate.
units: <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 11a">Ab. Zar. 11ᵃ</cite> sq. <he>איזהו עיקור … המְנַשֵּׁר פרסותיה וכ׳</he> what mutilation of an animal’s feet does not affect its vitality (v. <cite ref="I00811"><he>טְרֵפָה</he></cite>)? Cutting the tendons of its hoofs beneath the ankle; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 13a">ib. 13ᵃ</cite>.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 31:1">Pesik. R. s. 31</cite> <he>מְנַשְּׁרִים בשערו</he> they pluck his hair.
